props.doc:
Run analyst-authored Python in a child process under real limits.

This is the inner half of the isolation boundary; the outer half is the
container the sandbox pool runs in, which has no route to Postgres and no
default route off its network. Neither half is sufficient alone, and the
result records exactly which limits were applied - a platform that cannot
enforce a CPU quota on a given host should say so on the step rather than
imply a guarantee it did not deliver.
props.name: run_isolated

props.code:
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time

applied = {"wall_clock": True, "output_cap": True, "argv_launch": True,
           "scrubbed_env": True, "cpu": False, "address_space": False,
           "processes": False, "file_size": False}

preamble = [
    "import json, sys",
    "try:",
    "    import resource",
    "    resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_CPU, (%d, %d))"
    % (limits["cpu_seconds"], limits["cpu_seconds"]),
    "    resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_AS, (%d, %d))"
    % (limits["address_space_mb"] * 1048576, limits["address_space_mb"] * 1048576),
    "    resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_NPROC, (%d, %d))"
    % (limits["max_processes"], limits["max_processes"]),
    "    resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_FSIZE, (%d, %d))"
    % (limits["max_file_size_mb"] * 1048576, limits["max_file_size_mb"] * 1048576),
    "except ImportError:",
    "    pass",
    "inputs = json.loads(sys.stdin.read())",
    "",
]
epilogue = ["", "sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({'__result__': run(inputs)}))"]

program = "\n".join(preamble) + source + "\n".join(epilogue)

# Argv launch, shell=False, always. The platform never builds a shell string,
# anywhere, which is what makes command injection a structural non-issue.
environment = {"PATH": "/usr/bin:/bin", "HOME": "/tmp", "LANG": "C.UTF-8",
               "PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE": "1", "PYTHONHASHSEED": "0"}

started = time.time()
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as workdir:
    try:
        completed = subprocess.run(
            [sys.executable, "-I", "-S", "-c", program],
            input=json.dumps(inputs),
            capture_output=True, text=True, shell=False,
            cwd=workdir, env=environment,
            timeout=limits["wall_clock_ms"] / 1000.0,
            start_new_session=True,
        )
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        return {"ok": False, "limits_applied": applied,
                "error": {"error_class": "TRANSIENT",
                          "message": "exceeded the wall-clock limit and was killed"}}

if os.name == "posix":
    applied.update({"cpu": True, "address_space": True,
                    "processes": True, "file_size": True})

cap = limits["max_output_bytes"]
stdout = completed.stdout[:cap]
truncated = len(completed.stdout) > cap

if completed.returncode != 0:
    return {"ok": False, "limits_applied": applied,
            "logs": completed.stderr[:cap].splitlines()[-50:],
            "error": {"error_class": "PERMANENT",
                      "message": "exited with code %d" % completed.returncode}}

try:
    parsed = json.loads(stdout)["__result__"]
except (ValueError, KeyError):
    return {"ok": False, "limits_applied": applied,
            "error": {"error_class": "VALIDATION",
                      "message": "the command did not return a JSON object from run()"}}

return {"ok": True, "output": parsed, "limits_applied": applied,
        "truncated": truncated,
        "duration_ms": int((time.time() - started) * 1000),
        "logs": completed.stderr[:cap].splitlines()[-50:]}
